[[File:Folkman as subdivided double.svg|thumb|The [[Folkman graph]] (red subdivision vertices and blue doubled vertices) as the subdivided double of a five-vertex complete graph (yellow)]]
In [[graph theory]], the '''subdivided double''' is a construction used to transform a [[Quartic graph|4-regular graph]] into a larger 4-regular graph. It consists of two steps: subdividing every edge into a path of two edges (with a new vertex in the middle of each path), and then replacing every vertex of the original graph with two copies, both adjacent to the same subdivision vertices.{{r|pw07|pw14}} Potočnik, Verret, and Wilson use the notation <math>\operatorname{SDD}(G)</math> to denote the subdivided double of a graph <math>G</math>.{{r|pvw}} It was named as the subdivided double earlier, by Potočnik and Wilson.{{r|pw07}}

An example of a subdivided double is the [[Folkman graph]], a ten-vertex graph that can be constructed from the five-vertex complete graph <math>K_5</math> as its subdivided double <math>\operatorname{SDD}(K_5)</math>.{{r|pw14}}

Every subdivided double is a [[bipartite graph]], with the subdivision vertices on one side of its bipartition and the doubled vertices on the other side.{{r|pw07}} When the starting graph <math>G</math> is an [[arc-transitive graph]] (having symmetries mapping any two [[orientation (graph theory)|oriented edges]] to each other), the subdivided double <math>\operatorname{SDD}(G)</math> is an [[edge-transitive graph]]: the subdivided double has symmetries that map any two edges to each other. However, it may not be arc-transitive or [[vertex-transitive graph|vertex-transitive]]: there may be no symmetry that swaps the two sides of the bipartition. For this reason, the subdivided double construction has been studied as a way of generating [[semi-symmetric graph]]s, bipartite graphs that are edge-transitive but not vertex-transitive.{{r|pw07|pw14}} Every subdivided double has exponentially many [[Hamiltonian cycle]]s, and in a subdivided double every Hamiltonian cycle is complementary to another Hamiltonian cycle, forming a [[Hamiltonian decomposition]].{{r|epp}}

Whenever a 4-regular semi-symmetric graph contains two twin vertices, vertices that have the same sets of neighbors as each other, it can be constructed as a subdivided double.{{r|pw07|pw14}}
